newsitem.title: GERMANY: German, Japanese firms should cooperate more - Ifo.
newsitem.headline: German, Japanese firms should cooperate more - Ifo.

text.p: German and Japanese firms should step up their cooperation because experience shows both can benefit, particularly if they join forces to enter markets in China and Southeast Asia, the Ifo economic institute said.
In 1997, there were 80 cases of German-Japanese cooperation in third countries, mainly in the automobile and components industries, Ifo said in a study to be published on Monday.
A total of 62 of those ventures were aimed at developing and expanding markets and the most important motive for cooperation was to share costs and risk, Ifo said.
"The companies that succeed in overcoming the problems in dealing with a firm from another culture can achieve decisive advantages in international competition," Ifo said.

It added that it suspected that German companies were less willing to cooperate than Japanese due to differences in mentality and difficulties encountered by German firms in obtaining information about prospective Japanese partners.
In some cases, German firms also feared being taken over by their partner, Ifo said.
